decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line that has survived its first year in the portfolio, it likely meets minimum aspirations and a large established producer would normally continue backing it.
The comfort insole still supports cross-selling with the core footwear business, but after already pruning one insole the firm would watch this more closely for overlap and below-aspiration results.

The ergonomic safety-shoe series has clear strategic visibility and strong fit with the firm's main capabilities, so management would usually give it further time unless performance clearly disappoints.
Firefighter and rescue boots remain a plausible niche extension of the firm's protective-footwear competence, though their narrower market makes them more droppable if demand stays below aspiration.
Because the moulded insole is a flagship product linked to the firm's innovation direction, management would be very unlikely to withdraw it quickly and would more likely keep refining it.
